newsitem.title: UK: Don't leave us just yet, Poland tells EBRD.
newsitem.headline: Don't leave us just yet, Poland tells EBRD.

text.p: Poland, one of the former Soviet bloc's top economic success stories, told the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on Tuesday it should continue to remain active in the country.

Responding to western suggestions that the most advanced central and eastern European countries -- Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia -- were close to "graduation" from the pool of countries requiring EBRD assistance, Polish National Bank Governor Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said:

"Even in the most advanced countries in transition, there is still a great demand for the Bank's financing in areas where it can be additional, having significant transition impact and meeting sound banking criteria."
"Despite our progress in the market transition, the EBRD still has room to expand in Poland," she added.

The EBRD, set up in 1991 to assist former communist countries in becoming market economies, has gradually been shifting the focus of its activities further east into less developed regions, mainly in the former Soviet Union.

Gronkiewicz-Waltz, speaking at the EBRD's annual meeting in London, said any geographic shift in the Bank's operations should take place gradually "in order to maintain portfolio balance, credit quality and profitability."
"We believe that the job of graduation should be left mostly to the markets," she added.

Britain's representative Lynda Chalker earlier told the annual meeting that as Poland and other countries prepared for membership of the European Union, "it is timely to start thinking about their eventual graduation from the Bank."
